brief.headline: A Record Flagship Is Not a Fundraising Recovery
bullets: Fundraising: Advent closed the largest buyout fund to finish raising in 2026 so far.
Earnings & AUM: A rare Monday earnings report for Apple will give investors a glimpse into how new CEO John Ternus is managing inflated memory prices and a tougher backdrop for consumer spending.
Infrastructure & Energy: Open questions like Iran and tariffs and stubbornly high interest rates will all have their fingerprints on the electoral outcome.

Private Credit: Blue Owl Capital has reported a decline in redemption requests at its flagship private credit fund for the second consecutive quarter, as investor demand for withdrawals continued to ease in Q3.

AI & Technology: The bottleneck in the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout is neither capital nor demand, but rather the operational capability to develop land, secure a grid connection, and build the power supply, says Brookfield Asset Management CEO Connor Teskey on Goldman Sachs Exchanges: Great Investors.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,743.98 (up 0.3% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 17.2, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 4.98% (down 7 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.38 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.26%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: Blue Owl private credit redemption requests fall again in Q3
items.takeaway: Blue Owl Capital has reported a decline in redemption requests at its flagship private credit fund for the second consecutive quarter, as investor demand for withdrawals continued to ease in Q3.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer withdrawal requests suggest investors are growing more comfortable with private credit, which eases pressure on managers to sell assets to pay them out.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.26%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 30.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.

items.title: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators
items.takeaway: The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012.
items.whyItMatters: Signs of strain in private credit are an early warning for its investors: more defaults or deferred interest would cut income and push down the value of the loans.
